messages.author: 14f33f5ab5b4a1db
messages.subject: How do I convert this inla() call to a bru() call?
parts:
I have been trying to convert my inla call to a bru call to use some of the inlabru wrappers like generate() and predict(), but am having some issues. My model looks like this:

```
model <- inla(target ~ 1

    + fixed_effect_1
    + fixed_effect_2
    + fixed_effect_3
    + fixed_effect_4
    + fixed_effect_5
    + fixed_effect_6
    + fixed_effect_7

    # Random Effects
    + f(random_effect_1, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_1)
    + f(random_effect_2, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_2)
    + f(random_effect_3, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_3)
    + f(random_effect_4, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_4)
    + f(random_effect_5, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_5)
    + f(random_effect_6, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_6)
    + f(random_effect_7, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_7)
    + f(random_effect_8, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_8)
   
    , data=modeling_df, family="T"
    , control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, po=TRUE, config=TRUE)
    , control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive",  int.strategy="auto", cmin=0)
    , verbose=F
)
```

I have tried various ways, but do not think I am close to getting it to work. How can I convert this to a bru() call?

Thank you.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How do I convert this inla() call to a bru() call?
parts:
Hi,
that model should only need very minor changes:
(For speed of writing I call the effects rf#, but you could also call them
random_effect_#, so that other post-processing code you have
wouldn't need to change;
I assume your actual model has different names for all of the components...)

```
model <- bru(~ Intercept(1)

+ fixed_effect_1
+ fixed_effect_2
+ fixed_effect_3
+ fixed_effect_4
+ fixed_effect_5
+ fixed_effect_6
+ fixed_effect_7

# Random Effects

+ rf1(random_effect_1, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_1)
+ rf2(random_effect_2, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_2)
+ rf3(random_effect_3, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_3)
+ rf4(random_effect_4, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_4)
+ rf5(random_effect_5, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_5)
+ rf6(random_effect_6, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_6)
+ rf7(random_effect_7, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_7)
+ rf8(random_effect_8, model='iid', hyper=hyper_random_effect_8),
like(
formula = target ~ .,
data=modeling_df, family="T"
),
options = list(
control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, po=TRUE),
control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="auto", cmin=0),

verbose=FALSE
)
)
```

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How do I convert this inla() call to a bru() call?
parts:
Yes, bru is more picky about the inputs and the default component mappings don’t accept missing covariates. In plain inla, those are treated as “zero effect”, which can
either be achieved by a custom mapper that allows that (I’ll add that to the default mapper to iid models ), or by replacing the NA by e.g. 1, and adding a
weights=!is.na(original_covariate)
argument to the component definition.
The latter method is available right now.
Once I’ve updated the default iid mapper that will be available in the development version.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How do I convert this inla() call to a bru() call?
parts:
No, it should all be part of each individual component definition;

~ ... + your_component_label(input_without_na, weights =
!is.na(original_input_with_na), model = "iid", ...)

It also depends a bit on _why_ you have NAs in your random effect
indices. The method above only applies to the specific case where you
want an NA to lead to "effect = zero".

The reason inlabru doesn't (yet) have that behaviour is that it risks
masking problems where there wasn't supposed to be any missing
covariate values, and then giving effect zero without warning leads to
hard to track down errors in the statistical analysis. For purely
indexed component types like iid however, it's a different situation
than for may other types of covariates, so the risk of allowing this
behaviour should be smaller, and there are valid use cases. In the
future however, there will be more complex inlabru component types
where the above explicit !is.na() solution will be a much clearer
solution than special treatment of NAs, so we'll see how this evolves.
It would help to get some information about your specific use case, so
we can take valid use cases into account when developing the interface
further.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How do I convert this inla() call to a bru() call?
parts:
In the CRAN inlabru version (2.6.0) you can probably already simplify
your code by just doing this:

~ ... + comp_label(input_with_na, model="iid", mapper =
bru_mapper_index(n = max(input_with_na, na.rm = TRUE)), ...)

In the development version, I've just modified the default mapper to
allow NA inputs to generate effect zero, so if you install from github
(or in about an hour or so, from
https://inlabru-org.r-universe.dev/ui#package:inlabru when it builds
version 2.6.0.9003) you shouldn't need to do anything special to get
the NA --> zero effects.

Finn
